BURSEVI:v10p383/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p383/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p383/r1.claim: Al-‘adiyat is the plural of a swift-running creature; its yā’ replaces wāw because of the preceding kasra, and the oath concerns horses racing toward the enemy.
BURSEVI:v10p383/r1.anchor: وهي الجارية بسرعة من القدر وهو بالفارسية دويدن

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas withdrew his earlier position and returned to Ali’s interpretation.
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس فنزعت عن قولي ورجعت إلى الذي قال علي

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r3.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the oath’s runners as camels.
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله {والعاديات ضبحا} قال: الإبل

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r4.claim: Ibrahim transmits Ali’s view that the runners are camels.
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r4.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب: هي الإبل

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies them as horses.
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هي الخيل فبلغ عليا قول ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r6.claim: Ali objects that they had no horses at Badr, apart from al-Miqdad’s piebald mount.
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r6.anchor: وقال علي: كذبت يا ابن فلانة والله ما كان معنا يوم بدر فارس إلا المقداد وكان على فرس أبلق

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the horses belonged to a separate detachment.
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إنما كان ذلك في سرية بعثت

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r8.claim: In the debate, Ali again says the oath refers to camels.

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas argues that the runners raise dust with their hooves.
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r9.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: ألا ترى أنها تثير نقعا فما شيء تثيره إلا بحوافرها

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas, transmitted by Mujahid, says the oath is about horses.
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r10.anchor: مجاهد عن ابن عباس {والعاديات ضبحا} قال: الخيل

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas places the oath in battle, while Ibn Masud places it in pilgrimage.
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r16.anchor: قال ابن عباس في القتال وقال ابن مسعود: في الحج

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas says only a dog or horse among animals makes the described panting sound.
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r17.anchor: عن ابن عباس {والعاديات ضبحا} قال: ليس بشيء من الدواب يضبح إلا كلب أو فرس

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r22.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r22.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r22.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr instead says the runners are camels.
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r22.anchor: قال عمرو: وكان عبيد بن عمير يقول: هي الإبل

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r23.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r23.claim: Ibn Abbas defines the horse’s ḍabḥ by the sound it makes while running, likened to “ah, ah.”
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r23.anchor: عن ابن عباس {والعاديات ضبحا} قال: الخيل ضبحها زجرها ألم تر أن الفرس إذا عدا قال: أح أح فذاك ضبحها

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r1.claim: Ali distinguishes a horse’s panting or neighing from a camel’s breathing.
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r1.anchor: عن علي قال: الضبح من الخيل الحمحمة ومن الإبل النفس

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r2.claim: Qatada reads the passage as horses running until panting, striking sparks with their hooves, raiding at dawn, raising dust, entering the people’s gathering; kanud means ungrateful.
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {والعاديات ضبحا} قال: هي الخيل تعدو حتى تضبح

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r3.claim: Mujahid says these are horses, whose panting can be heard when run, unlike camels.
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد {والعاديات ضبحا} قال: الخيل ألم تر إلى الفرس إذا أجري كيف يضبح وما ضبح بعير قط

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r9.speaker: عطية
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r9.claim: Atiyya identifies the runners as horses and describes their effort as panting or groaning as they run.
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r9.anchor: عن عطية {والعاديات ضبحا} قال: الخيل ألم ترها إذا عدت تزحر يقول تنحر

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r20.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r20.claim: Ibn Masud interprets the oath as camels on pilgrimage.
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r20.anchor: عن ابن مسعود {والعاديات ضبحا} قال: هي الإبل في الحج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r1.claim: The first three descriptions are joined by fa, the usual Arabic pattern for successive adjectives or places; it usually marks sequential occurrence here and in Ibn Ziyaba's verse, but may mark mention order in al-Saffat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r1.anchor: وعطفت هذه الأوصاف الثلاثة الأولى بالفاء لأن أسلوب العرب في عطف الصفات وعطف الأمكنة أن يكون بالفاء

TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the charging creatures as horses.
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله {والعاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] قال: الخيل

TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r2.speaker: غير ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r2.claim: A view attributed to someone other than Ibn Abbas identifies them as camels.
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r2.anchor: وزعم غير ابن عباس أنها الإبل

TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r3.claim: A report through Mujahid says Ibn Abbas understood the oath to concern fighting.
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {والعاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] قال ابن عباس: «هو في القتال»

TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r4.claim: Ikrima points to a horse's panting while it runs as the meaning of dabhan.
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r4.anchor: قال: سئل عكرمة، عن قوله: {والعاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] قال: «ألم تر إلى الفرس إذا جرى كيف يضبح»

TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r5.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r5.claim: Ata says only a dog and a horse make the sound called dabhan.
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r5.anchor: عن عطاء، قال: «ليس شيء من الدواب يضبح غير الكلب والفرس»

TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r6.claim: Mujahid says the charging horses pant as they run.
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {والعاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] قال: «الخيل تضبح»

TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r7.claim: Qatadah describes horses running until they pant.
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {والعاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] قال: «هي الخيل، عدت حتى ضبحت»

TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r8.speaker: سالم
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r8.claim: Salim reads the verse and explains it as horses running while panting.
TAB-FULL:v24p570#2/r8.anchor: قال: سمعت سالما، يقرأ: {والعاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] قال: «هي الخيل عدت ضبحا»

TAB-FULL:v24p572/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r1.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r1.claim: Ata identifies the charging creatures as horses.
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r1.anchor: عن واصل، عن عطاء، {والعاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] قال: «الخيل»

TAB-FULL:v24p572/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says no animal has ever panted in this manner except a dog or horse.
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «ما ضبحت دابة قط إلا كلب أو فرس»

TAB-FULL:v24p572/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the charging creatures as horses.
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r3.anchor: سمعت أبا معاذ، يقول: أخبرنا عبيد، قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: والعاديات ضبحا قال: «هي الخيل»

TAB-FULL:v24p572/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r4.claim: Another report identifies the charging creatures as horses.
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r4.anchor: عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس، قال: «هي الخيل»

TAB-FULL:v24p572/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r5.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r5.claim: A report from Abdullah identifies the charging creatures as camels; Ibrahim transmits the same interpretation.
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r5.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن إبراهيم، عن عبد الله، {والعاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] قال: هي الإبل

TAB-FULL:v24p572/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وعلي
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r6.claim: In a conversation with Ali, Ibn Abbas first says the oath concerns horses raiding for God's cause and lighting cooking fires at night; Ali counters that Badr had only two horses and identifies the creatures as pilgrims' camels moving from Arafat through Muzdalifa to Mina, and Ibn Abbas recants.
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، حدثه قال: " بينما أنا في الحجر جالس، أتاني رجل يسأل عن {العاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] فقلت له: الخيل حين تغير في سبيل الله

TAB-FULL:v24p575/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r1.claim: Ibrahim again reports the interpretation that the charging creatures are camels.
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r1.anchor: عن منصور، عن إبراهيم، {والعاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] قال: الإبل

TAB-FULL:v24p575/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r2.claim: Mujahid transmits Ibn Masud's view that the verse concerns the pilgrimage.
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {والعاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] قال: قال ابن مسعود: هو في الحج

TAB-FULL:v24p575/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r3.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r3.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr says the charging creatures are camels.
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r3.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير، قال: " هي الإبل، يعني {والعاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] "

TAB-FULL:v24p575/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers horses because camels do not pant, whereas the verse explicitly describes panting while running.
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r4.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك عندي بالصواب: قول من قال: عني بالعاديات: الخيل، وذلك أن الإبل لا تضبح، وإنما تضبح الخيل

TAB-FULL:v24p575/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r5.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r5.claim: Ali distinguishes horse panting as a whinny-like sound and camel panting as breath.
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r5.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه: " الضبح من الخيل: الحمحمة، ومن الإبل: النفس "

TAB-FULL:v24p575/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas imitates the sound of panting as ‘ah ah.’
TAB-FULL:v24p575/r6.anchor: عن عطاء، قال: سمعت ابن عباس، " يصف الضبح: أح أح "

TAB-FULL:v24p576/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p576/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p576/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the horses raid for God's cause, then return at night so their riders prepare food and kindle a fire.
TAB-FULL:v24p576/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: سألني علي بن أبي طالب رضى الله عنه، عن {العاديات ضبحا} [العاديات: 1] {فالموريات قدحا} [العاديات: 2] فقلت له: الخيل تغير في سبيل الله، ثم تأوي إلى الليل

TAB-FULL:v24p579/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p579/r7.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v24p579/r7.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam used to decline interpreting these letters and said they form an oath sworn by God.
TAB-FULL:v24p579/r7.anchor: وقد كان زيد بن أسلم يذكر تفسير هذه الأحرف ويأباها، ويقول: إنما هو قسم أقسم الله به

TAB-FULL:v24p580/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r6.claim: In Ali's interpretation of the oath as pilgrims' camels, the dust arises as animals tread the ground with hooves and feet between Arafat, Muzdalifa, and Mina.
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: قال لي علي: " إنما العاديات ضبحا من عرفة إلى المزدلفة، ومن المزدلفة إلى منى

THALABI:v10p269/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p269/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p269/r1.claim: Another version identifies the horse in the preceding account as belonging to Mirthad ibn Abi Mirthad al-Ghanawi.
THALABI:v10p269/r1.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى وفرس لمرثد بن أبي مرثد الغنوي

THALABI:v10p269/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p269/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p269/r2.claim: He first says the chargers are horses raiding in God’s cause, then returning at night to prepare food and kindle a fire.
THALABI:v10p269/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس حدثه قال: بينما أنا في الحجر جالس أتاني رجل فسأل عن العاديات ضبحا، فقال له: الخيل

THALABI:v10p269/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p269/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
THALABI:v10p269/r3.claim: Ali rejects the horse interpretation because at Badr, Islam’s first expedition, the Muslims had only two horses; he says the chargers are camels from Arafat to Muzdalifa and Mina.
THALABI:v10p269/r3.anchor: والله إن كانت لأول غزوة في الإسلام بدر، وما كان معنا إلا فرسان

THALABI:v10p269/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p269/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p269/r4.claim: After hearing Ali’s argument, Ibn Abbas withdrew his interpretation and adopted Ali’s view; Ibn Masud, Muhammad ibn Umayr, Muhammad ibn Kab, and al-Suddi also held it.
THALABI:v10p269/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فنزعت عن قولي ورجعت إلى الذي قال علي

THALABI:v10p269/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p269/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p269/r5.claim: The account says a camel reading takes dabḥa as stretched necks during travel, treating ḍabaḥa and ḍabaʿa as synonyms and citing Safiyya’s poem.
THALABI:v10p269/r5.anchor: وضبحت وضبعت بمعنى واحد، قالت صفية بنت عبد المطلب

TABATABAI:100:6-11/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r10.speaker: مقاتل
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r10.claim: One account says the Prophet sent a company against a clan of Kinana led by al-Mundhir ibn Amr; when they were late, hypocrites assumed they had all been killed, and the sura revealed their horses' charge.
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r10.anchor: قيل بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سرية إلى حي من كنانة فاستعمل عليهم المنذر بن عمرو الأنصاري أحد النقباء فتأخر رجوعهم

TABATABAI:100:6-11/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r11.claim: Another reported occasion says the sura came down after the Prophet sent Ali to Dhat al-Salasil, where he defeated the enemy after earlier companions had returned unsuccessful.
TABATABAI:100:6-11/r11.anchor: وقيل نزلت السورة لما بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عليا عليه السلام إلى ذات السلاسل فأوقع بهم وذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after the Prophet sent cavalry away for a month without news, the opening of al-Adiyat was revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خيلا فاستمرت شهرا لا ياتيه منها خبر فنزلت : والعاديات ضبحا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p321/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p321/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود وجابر والحسن وعكرمة وعطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p321/r12.claim: Ibn Masud, Jabir, al-Hasan, Ikrima, and Ata classify Surat al-Adiyat as Meccan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p321/r12.anchor: مكية في قول ابن مسعود وجابر والحسن وعكرمة وعطاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p321/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p321/r13.speaker: ابن عباس وأنس بن مالك وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p321/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas, Anas ibn Malik, and Qatada classify it as Medinan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p321/r13.anchor: ومدينة في قول ابن عباس وأنس بن مالك وقتادة

RAZI-FULL:v32p60/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p60/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p60/r1.claim: The author identifies al-ʿAdiyat as a Meccan surah of eleven verses.

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Riddling that creates rhetorical tension also structures oath sequences such as Q 100 and teaching questions at 90:12–16, 97:2–4, 101:1–11, and 104:5–9.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: auf dem Einsatz von Änigmatisierung zur Erzeugung rhetorischer Spannung basieren aber auch Schwurserien wie zu Beginn von Q 100

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r1.claim: Al-ʿādiyāt means running and describes war horses, since the four following adjectives suit them; the camels of Muzdalifah interpretation has no corroboration and does not fit those adjectives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r1.anchor: means “to run.” Here it is mentioned as an adjective

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r2.claim: The alternative that the word means warriors' horses is unsupported, especially because it leaves the oath unrelated to verse 6's assertion that man is ungrateful to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r2.anchor: What relationship can these words of the muqsam ‘alayh have with the horses of the warriors and the combatants?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r3.claim: Both alternative readings wrongly assume that oath objects must be sacred; Islahi rejects that assumption and says the real point is their testimony.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p415/r3.anchor: Both these interpretations are based on the false notion that it is essential that things which are sworn by should be sacred.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216#2/r3.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216#2/r3.claim: A report says Ali identifies the oath animals as pilgrims' camels: they run from Arafat to Muzdalifa, light fires there, then hurry at dawn to Mina; dust is raised by their feet. Ibn Abbas initially said war horses, then adopted Ali's answer after Ali noted only two horses were present at Badr.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216#2/r3.anchor: إنما العاديات ضبحا الإبل تعد من عرفة إلى المزدلفة فإذا أوو إلى المزدلفة أوروا النيران

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216#2/r4.claim: The Badr objection does not establish that the verse refers to that battle: Ibn Abbas may mean horses generally, or a particular delayed expedition; the proposed defense based on Badr's special status is very weak. The report is likely unsound, al-Hakim is often too lenient, and transmissions conflict over Ali's interpretation; horses better raise dust, while the report implies both horses and camels plus warriors or pilgrims.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216#2/r4.anchor: والأحرى أن الخبر لا صحة له وتصحيح الحاكم محكوم عليه عند أهل الأثر بكثرة التساهل فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p217/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p217/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p217/r1.claim: Esoteric readings make the charging creatures longing souls: their prayer sounds from yearning, thought kindles lights of knowledge, and they charge desire and habit toward sacred light, stirring longing to reach the ranks of the exalted.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p217/r1.anchor: أن يكون المقسم به النفوس العادية أثر كما لهن الموريات بأفكارهن أنوار المعارف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p217/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p217/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p217/r2.claim: A second mystical interpretation maps the verse onto spiritual struggle: dhikr kindles guidance in the body, the soul crosses bodily darkness into the dawn of the self, stirs passing thoughts, then centers the heart's forces in the army of remembrance.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p217/r2.anchor: الموريات بحوافر الذكر نار الهداية المستكنة فى حجر القالب وقت تخمير اللطيفة

BINTSHATI:v1p119/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p119/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p119/r3.claim: She finds a striking, previously unnoticed connection between the opening violent raid and the closing scene of graves and hearts laid bare.
BINTSHATI:v1p119/r3.anchor: وهذه الوقفة الحاسمة، يبلغ بها القرآن ذروة المشهد العنيف لبعثرة ما في القبور وتحصيل ما في الصدور

BINTSHATI:v1p119/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p119/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p119/r4.claim: The surah opens by evoking the familiar sudden raid at dawn, before its targets notice the raiders have entered and scattered their gathering in dust.
BINTSHATI:v1p119/r4.anchor: تبدأ بواو لبقسم لافته في قوة إلى المشهد المألوف، لإغارة عنيفة مفاجئة

BINTSHATI:v1p119/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p119/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p119/r5.claim: A familiar raid's panic provides an image for the unseen resurrection: people are scattered from graves, depart in groups, and face rapid, linked events culminating before the All-Aware.
BINTSHATI:v1p119/r5.anchor: ذلك هو مشهد البعث، يباغت القوم - وقد طال ما جحدوا نعمة الله وغرتهم الأماني -

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508/r1.claim: Al-ʿĀdiyāt warns that most people will perish on the earthquake day because they prefer transient status and wealth over what lasts with the Lord; its oath and subject signal this purpose.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508/r1.anchor: أكثر الخلق يوم الزلزلة هالك لإيثار الفاني من العز والمال على الباقي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508/r2.claim: The chapter's name most clearly points to its subject through reflection on the oath and what is sworn to.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508/r2.anchor: وقد علم أن اسمها أدل شيء على ذلك لما هدى إليه القسم والمقسم عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508/r3.claim: The basmala describes God's complete command, universal gifts of creation and clarification, and special completion of blessing for His elect through guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508/r3.anchor: الذي له الأمر كله فلا يسأل عما يفعل

QASHANI:100:1-4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:100:1-4/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:100:1-4/r1.claim: The chargers represent striving souls traveling God's path through ascetic discipline, strenuous effort, and the breathless intensity of longing.
QASHANI:100:1-4/r1.anchor: النفوس المجتهدة السائرة في سبيل الله التي تعدو من شدة سيرها ورياضتها

QASHANI:100:1-4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:100:1-4/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:100:1-4/r2.claim: Their panting is the exhalation of longing's ardor.

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r1.claim: The basmala is a jealous word: only a tongue protected from idle talk and backbiting may utter it, and only a guarded heart may know it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r1.anchor: كلمة غيور لا يصلح لذكرها إلا لسان مصون

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r2.claim: Only a spirit protected from attachments and veils is fit to love the basmala.
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r2.anchor: ولا يصلح لمحبتها إلا روح محفوظة عن العلاقة والحجبة

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r3.claim: The chargers are horses; panting is the sound of their bodies or breath under exertion.
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r3.anchor: الخيل التي تعدو . { ضبحا } أي إذا ضبحن ضبحا

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r4.claim: Another explanation takes the chargers to be camels.

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r5.claim: Another explanation identifies them as the horses of raiders.

FARRA:v3p284#2/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p284#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v3p284#2/r1.claim: The chargers are horses, and their panting is the sound of their breathing as they run.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#11/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#11/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#11/r1.claim: The chargers are horses, and dhabḥ is the sound from their throats as they run.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#11/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#11/r2.speaker: علي
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#11/r2.claim: Ali identifies the chargers as camels going to Badr and notes that the Muslims had only al-Miqdad's horse.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#11/r2.anchor: هي الإبل تذهب إلى وقعة بدر

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#11/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#11/r3.speaker: آخرون
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#11/r3.claim: Others treat ḍabʿ and ḍabḥ as equivalent words for a camel's sound while moving; the she-camel may be called either ḍabaʿat or ḍabaḥat.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#11/r3.anchor: و "الضبح" واحد في السير؛ يقال: ضبعت الناقة وضبحت

MAJAZ:v2p307/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p307/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p307/r1.claim: The chargers are horses; ḍabḥ and ḍabʿ are equivalent, while another explanation takes it as panting or breathing, with an implicit subject.

NAHHAS:v5p277/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p277/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p277/r1.claim: The oath particle wa governs the genitive; scholars disagree whether the chargers are horses or camels.
NAHHAS:v5p277/r1.anchor: خفض بواو القسم وللعلماء في معناها قولان

NAHHAS:v5p277/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p277/r2.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة عن ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p277/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, as reported by Mujahid and Ikrima, identifies the chargers as horses.
NAHHAS:v5p277/r2.anchor: روى مجاهد وعكرمة عن ابن عباس أنها الخيل

NAHHAS:v5p277/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p277/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
NAHHAS:v5p277/r3.claim: Ali identifies the chargers as camels, arguing Badr had only two horses and describing their pilgrimage route from Arafat through Muzdalifa to Mina.
NAHHAS:v5p277/r3.anchor: إن أول غزوة كانت لبدر وما كان معنا إلا فرسان فرس للزبير وفرس للمقداد بن الأسود

NAHHAS:v5p277/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p277/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
NAHHAS:v5p277/r4.claim: Ibn Masud also says the chargers are camels.
NAHHAS:v5p277/r4.anchor: إنما العاديات من عرفة إلى المزدلفة ومن المزدلفة إلى منى

NAHHAS:v5p277/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p277/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p277/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses dhabḥ as the animals' blowing through their lips.
NAHHAS:v5p277/r11.anchor: وعن ابن عباس الضبح نفخها بمشافرها

NAHHAS:v5p277/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p277/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p277/r15.claim: Dhabḥan functions as an adverb of time.

SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r1.claim: Al-ʿadiyat is the feminine plural active participle of running quickly; its yāʾ replaces wāw after a kasra, as in ghaziyat from ghazw.
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r1.anchor: وهي الجارية بسرعة، من العدو، وهو المشي بسرعة

SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r2.claim: One analysis makes ḍabḥan an emphatic verbal noun for the active participle and a type of running; Abu Ubayda and al-Mubarrad derive it from extending the forearm in hard running, with ḥ replacing ʿayn.
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r2.anchor: مصدر مؤكد لاسم الفاعل؛ فإن الضبح نوع من السير والعدو

SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة والمبرد
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Mubarrad connect panting to extending the animals' forearms as they run.
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r3.anchor: قالا الضبح من إضباعها في السير

SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r4.speaker: عنترة
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r4.claim: ʿAntara's verse uses ḍabḥ to describe horses in the pools of death.
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r4.anchor: قال عنترة: 4617 والخيل تعلم حين تض

SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r5.claim: A second analysis treats ḍabḥan as a circumstantial verbal noun: horses panting or possessing panting, a chest sound distinct from neighing.
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r5.anchor: مصدر في موضع الحال، أي: ضابحات، أو ذوي ضبح

SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly mimicked the sound of panting as 'aḥ aḥ.'
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: انه حكاه فقال: أح أح

SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r7.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Abbas says only horses, dogs, and foxes pant.
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r7.anchor: ونقل عنه: أنه لم يضبح من الحيوان غير الخيل والكلب والثعلب

SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r8.claim: Ali rebukes the horse interpretation: Badr was the first campaign and had only two horses, while the chargers are camels traveling from Arafat through Muzdalifa to Mina.
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r8.anchor: ولم يكن معنا إلا فرسان: فرس للمقداد

SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r9.claim: If the camel report is authentic, al-Zamakhshari says panting is metaphorically applied to camels, as body-part terms are metaphorically applied to people and colts.
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r9.anchor: فإن صحت الرواية فقد استعير الضبح للإبل

SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r10.claim: Language authorities extend panting to camels, dark snakes, owls, echoes, hares, foxes, and bows; Abu Hanifa cites a bow's fox-like sound.
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r10.anchor: حنانة من نشم أو تالب تضبح في الكف ضباح الثعلب

SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r11.claim: These wider uses are metaphors: the word originates with the fox and was transferred to horses; panting derives from fire darkening color slightly.
SAMIN-DURR:100:1/r11.anchor: وعندي أن هذا من الاستعارة. ونقل أهل اللغة أن أصل الضبح في الثعلب

SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r1.claim: A third analysis supplies an omitted verb, 'they pant a panting'; that verb is circumstantial to the chargers.
SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r1.anchor: أن يكون منصوبا بفعل مقدر، أي: تضبح ضبحا

SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r2.claim: A fourth analysis makes ḍabḥan governed by al-ʿadiyat because panting necessarily accompanies running, as though the verse said 'the panting ones.'
SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r2.anchor: كأنه قيل: والضابحات لأن الضبح يكون مع العدو

SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r3.claim: The grammarian objects that if panting accompanies running, al-ʿadiyat should not itself be explained as 'the panting ones.'

SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r4.claim: The objection misreads al-Zamakhshari: 'as though it said' explains the inseparable relation and governance, not synonymy between running and panting.
SAMIN-DURR:100:1#2/r4.anchor: تفسير للتلازم، لا أنه هو هو

ASAD-NOTES:100:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:100:1#n1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:100:1#n1/r1.claim: Because the following clauses depict an imaginary parable, Asad prefers translating wa as 'Oh' rather than his usual 'Consider' or most translators' 'By.'
ASAD-NOTES:100:1#n1/r1.anchor: the subsequent clauses refer to a parabolic, imaginary situation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r1.claim: The oath sworn by horses is evidence for the later premise that man is ungrateful to his Lord.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r1.anchor: this oath sworn by the horses is a testimony to the ungratefulness of man

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r2.claim: Ḍabḥ is the sound from panting horses' nostrils; their exhausted state shows dutiful obedience and spending their last energy on their master's task.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r1.claim: Horses are singled out because clans needed high-pedigree warhorses for attack, defense, and family protection; their importance also made them common in classical poetry.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r1.anchor: they had great importance in launching an onslaught on the enemy

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r2.claim: The author cites a Ḥamāsī poet's verse about spending on a thoroughbred horse as a house sentinel and keeping a servant for it, illustrating horses' esteem.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p418/r2.anchor: I am restricting myself to just one couplet

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p390/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p390/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p390/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies the panting runners as horses that pant while running.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r1.claim: Al-ʿādiyāt describes swift runners, while exegetes dispute what is running; ḍabḥ is a loud sound during strenuous running, distinct from ordinary animal calls.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r1.anchor: العاديات: الجاريات بسرعة، وهو وصف، ويأتي في التفسير الخلاف في الموصوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is quoted as saying only horses and dogs pant, but Abū Ḥayyān doubts this attribution because Arabic applies ḍabḥ to many animals and even a bow.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: ليس يضبح من الحيوان غير الخيل والكلاب. قيل: ولا يصح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r3.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa's verse about a bow uses ḍabḥ for the bow's sound, likened to a fox.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r3.anchor: أنشد أبو حنيفة في صفة قوس: حنانة من نشم أو تألب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r4.claim: The word may originally describe a fox and be transferred to horses; it is linked to fire changing a color without fully burning it, or a slight darkening.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r4.anchor: وقال أهل اللغة: أصله للثعلب، فاستعير للخيل، وهو من ضبحته النار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda equates ḍabḥ and ḍabʿ with running very fast.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الضبح والضبع بمعنى العدو الشديد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r6.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives ḍabḥ from the horse's quick gait.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r6.anchor: وكذا قال المبرد: الضبح من إضباعها في السير.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r6.speaker: الجمهور من أهل التفسير واللغة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r6.claim: The majority of exegetes and linguists identify the runners as horses racing in God's way and panting as they run; ʿAntara's verse illustrates their panting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r6.anchor: والجمهور من أهل التفسير واللغة على أن العاديات هنا الخيل، تعدو في سبيل الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله وعلي وإبراهيم والسدي ومحمد بن كعب وعبيد بن عمير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r7.claim: These authorities identify the runners as pilgrims' camels charging from ʿArafāt and Muzdalifa during pilgrimage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله وعلي وإبراهيم والسدي ومحمد بن كعب وعبيد بن عمير: العاديات: الإبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r8.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r8.claim: ʿAlī argued for camels by citing Badr, where the Muslims had only two horses, and Ibn ʿAbbās then returned to his interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r8.anchor: وبهذا حج علي رضي الله عنه ابن عباس حين تماريا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r9.speaker: صفية بنت عبد المطلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r9.claim: Ṣafiyya bt. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib's verse depicts the pilgrims' runners at Jamʿ raising dust.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r9.anchor: وقالت صفية بنت عبد المطلب: فلا والعاديات غداة جمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r10.claim: Ḍabḥan is parsed as an omitted cognate verb, a circumstantial expression, or—following Abū ʿUbayda's gloss of running—as a cognate accusative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r10.anchor: وانتصب ضبحا على إضمار فعل، أي يضبحن ضبحا أو على أنه في موضع الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows ḍabḥan to modify al-ʿādiyāt as if the phrase meant panting runners; Abū Ḥayyān objects that panting and running are not identical.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p527/r11.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أو بالعاديات كأنه قيل: والضابحات

ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r1.claim: The majority identify al-ʿādiyāt as horses of raiders running swiftly for God's cause; the word derives from al-ʿādawāt with wāw changed to yāʾ after a kasra.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r1.anchor: والعاديات الجمهور على أنه قسم بخيل الغزاة في سبيل الله تعالى التي تعدو

ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r2.claim: Ḍabḥan is a verbal noun with an omitted verb and a circumstantial clause; it is the horses' breathing sound while running.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى ضبحا مصدر بفعله المحذوف أي تضبح أو يضبحن ضبحا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says horses make an ah-ah sound when running; ʿAlī says panting is a horse's ḥamḥama and a camel's breathing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر عن ابن عباس الخيل إذا عدت قالت أح أح

ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r4.claim: The commentary describes ḍabḥ as a loud sound during strenuous running, neither whinnying, growling, nor barking; it doubts Ibn ʿAbbās's restriction to horses and dogs.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r4.anchor: في البحر تصويت جهير عند العدو الشديد ليس بصهيل ولا رغاء ولا نباح

ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa's bow verse applies ḍabḥ to a bow's fox-like sound, supporting broader Arabic usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r5.anchor: أنشد أبو حنيفة في صفتها حنانة من نشم أو تالب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r6.speaker: عنترة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r6.claim: ʿAntara's verse applies panting to horses running in the waters of death.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r6.anchor: كما في قول عنترة والخيل تكدح حين تضبح في حياض الموت ضبحا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda equates ḍabḥ and ḍabʿ with running very fast, allowing ḍabḥan to function as a cognate accusative or a circumstantial expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p215/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة الضبح وكذا الضبع بمعنى العدو الشديد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء ومجاهد وعكرمة والحسن والكلبي وقتادة والمقاتلان وأبو العالية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r1.claim: These authorities identify al-ʿādiyāt as horses running in God's cause; ḍabḥ is the sound from their bodies while running.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وعطاء ومجاهد، وعكرمة، والحسن، والكلبي، وقتادة، والمقاتلان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says horses, dogs, and foxes pant when exhausted or frightened; the word relates to fire changing a color.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وليس شيء من الحيوانات تضبح غير الفرس والكلب والثعلب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r3.claim: Ḍabḥan is parsed as a cognate accusative, equivalent to saying the running horses pant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r3.anchor: نصب على المصدر، مجازه: والعاديات تضبح ضبحا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r4.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r4.claim: ʿAlī identifies al-ʿādiyāt as pilgrims' camels traveling from ʿArafāt to Muzdalifa and then Mina, and invokes Badr's two-horse force against the horse reading.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r4.anchor: وقال علي: هي الإبل في الحج، تعدو من عرفة إلى المزدلفة، ومن المزدلفة إلى منى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود ومحمد بن كعب والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Muḥammad b. Kaʿb, and al-Suddī also adopt the camel interpretation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r5.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب ابن مسعود، ومحمد بن كعب، والسدي.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r6.claim: Some camel interpreters explain ḍabḥan as the camels stretching their necks while moving.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p505#2/r6.anchor: يعني ضباحا تمد أعناقها في السير

BAYDAWI-FULL:100:1-5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:100:1-5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:100:1-5/r2.claim: The oath is by horses of raiders whose panting is their breath during running; ḍabḥan can be an omitted verb's object, cognate accusative, or circumstantial adjective.
BAYDAWI-FULL:100:1-5/r2.anchor: أقسم سبحانه بخيل الغزاة تعدو فتضبح ضبحا، وهو صوت أنفاسها عند العدو

BINTSHATI:v1p103/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p103/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p103/r4.claim: The usual oath reading treats the wāw as magnifying and emphasizing its object, which drives far-fetched interpretations.
BINTSHATI:v1p103/r4.anchor: الواو في أصل الاستعمال اللغوي للقسم، ويتجه به جمهور المفسرين إلى تعظيم ما يقسم به

BINTSHATI:v1p103/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p103/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
BINTSHATI:v1p103/r5.claim: Many commentators, including Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan, identify the runners as horses and restrict them to Muslim horses at Badr to explain the oath's honorific force.
BINTSHATI:v1p103/r5.anchor: فهي الخيل فيما ذهب كثير منهم، ولكي يستقيم لهم مفهوم بالقسم بها، تأولوها بخيول المسلمين

BINTSHATI:v1p104/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p104/r1.speaker: علي
BINTSHATI:v1p104/r1.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbās's report, ʿAlī challenges the horse reading because Badr was Islam's first battle and Muslims had only al-Zubayr's and al-Miqdād's horses; he says the runners are camels from ʿArafāt.
BINTSHATI:v1p104/r1.anchor: والله إن كانت لأول غزوة في الإسلام بدر، وما كان معنا إلا فرسان

BINTSHATI:v1p104/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p104/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI:v1p104/r2.claim: The reported camel interpretation describes pilgrims racing from ʿArafāt through Muzdalifa toward Mina and raising dust at Wādī Muḥassir.

BINTSHATI:v1p104/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p104/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BINTSHATI:v1p104/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd also interprets the runners as camels, a view followed by other commentators who emphasize the pilgrims' dignity.
BINTSHATI:v1p104/r3.anchor: إلى تفسيرها بالإبل، وتابعه على هذا عدد من المفسرين

BINTSHATI:v1p104/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p104/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p104/r7.claim: If the report from ʿAlī is authentic, al-Zamakhsharī says panting has been borrowed for camels as bodily terms are borrowed for humans.
BINTSHATI:v1p104/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: "إن صح ما روى عن

BINTSHATI:v1p105/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p105/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p105/r1.claim: The dispute remains unresolved, and Bint al-Shāṭiʾ attributes it to both sides' assumption that the oath must magnify its object, restricting the animals to warhorses or pilgrims' camels.
BINTSHATI:v1p105/r1.anchor: وهكذا يظل الخلاف دون أن ينحسم. فلكل قول رد، ولكل إعتراض جواب!

BINTSHATI:v1p105/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p105/r2.speaker: ابن القيم
BINTSHATI:v1p105/r2.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim says the horses need not be limited to raiders; the oath honors the noble animal through which people gain strength, victory, and vengeance on enemies.
BINTSHATI:v1p105/r2.anchor: فالقسم إنما وقع بما تضمنه شأن هذه العاديات من خلق هذا الحيوان

BINTSHATI:v1p105/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p105/r3.speaker: محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v1p105/r3.claim: Muḥammad ʿAbduh expands the horse interpretation as encouragement to value, acquire, train, and ride horses, prepare for defense, and excel in horsemanship.
BINTSHATI:v1p105/r3.anchor: لينوه بشأنها، ويعلى من قدرها في نفوس المؤمنين أهل العمل والجد

BINTSHATI:v1p105/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p105/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p105/r4.claim: As argued in her commentary on al-Ḍuḥā, the oath's wāw is more likely to have moved beyond its literal oath function for a rhetorical purpose.
BINTSHATI:v1p105/r4.anchor: وقد مضى القول، في تفسير سورة الضحى، بأن القسم بالواو هنا أقرب

BINTSHATI:v1p106/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p106/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p106/r2.claim: Al-ʿādiyāt occurs only here in the Qur'an; the root conveys distance and exceeding, reflected in swift running beyond ordinary pace, enmity's distance, and transgression beyond right.
BINTSHATI:v1p106/r2.anchor: الأصل اللغوي للعدو هو البعد والتجاوز، ومنه العدوة للمكان المتباعد

BINTSHATI:v1p106/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p106/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p106/r3.claim: Though horsemen can be called al-ʿādiyāt, ḍabḥ identifies horses themselves because it is their breathing sound when they run fast.
BINTSHATI:v1p106/r3.anchor: وقد يقال للفرسان عادية، لكن الضبح يعين أن المقصود بها هنا الخيل

BINTSHATI:v1p106/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p106/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p106/r4.claim: Ḍabḥan may be a cognate accusative with an omitted verb or a circumstantial adjective; Bint al-Shāṭiʾ prefers the verbal noun for its absolute, unrestricted sense.
BINTSHATI:v1p106/r4.anchor: لما فيها من معنى الإطلاق المحض

BINTSHATI:v1p106/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p106/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p106/r5.claim: The fāʾ linking mūriyāt to al-ʿādiyāt suggests causation: sparks result from hard running as the horses' hooves strike stones.
BINTSHATI:v1p106/r5.anchor: وعطف الموريات قدحا على العاديات ضبحا، بالفاء وفيها ملحظ السببية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r1.claim: The surah warns that most people will perish at the upheaval because they prefer fleeting status and wealth to what endures with God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r1.anchor: إعلام بأن أكثر الخلق يوم الزلزلة هالك لإيثار الفاني من العز والمال على الباقي عند ذي الجلال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r2.claim: The oath, its object, and what follows disclose this purpose; the title is especially apt because the oath and its answer point to it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r2.anchor: وقد علم أن اسمها أدل شيء على ذلك لما هدى إليه القسم والمقسم عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r3.claim: The title fits because the oath and its answer point to the surah's purpose.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r3.anchor: وقد علم أن اسمها أدل شيء على ذلك لما هدى إليه القسم والمقسم عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r4.claim: The basmala presents God as sovereign over all affairs, universally generous in creating and explaining, and specially merciful through guidance to His devoted servants.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#s100/r4.anchor: الذي عم بنعمة إيجاده وبيانه فنعمته أتم نعمة وأشمل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r1.claim: Following al-Zalzalah's account of judgment, this surah traces the disposition that produces evil deeds and the imagined worldly gain that sustains it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r1.anchor: ختم الزلزلة بالجزاء لأعمال الشر يوم الفصل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r2.claim: The oath rebukes people who fail to prepare for Judgment, prefer this life to the next, and treat God's blessings without gratitude.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r2.anchor: موبخا من لا يستعد لذلك اليوم بالاحتراز التام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r3.claim: Horses are the swift animals meant; their backs bring honor and their bellies wealth, but they earn sin when used for pride and harm and reward when used for God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r3.anchor: وهي الخيل التي ظهورها عز وبطونها كنز

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r4.claim: A horse used in God's cause, with its owner's due care for God's right upon it, becomes a source of protection and reward.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r4.anchor: ومن حمل عليها ولم ينس حق الله في رقابها وظهورها وكانت له سترا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r5.claim: The oath invites reflection on horses' distinctive secrets, which show that their distinguishing features were bestowed by the one sovereign agent; the oath is ultimately by God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r5.anchor: وإنما أقسم بها ليتأمل ما فيها من الأسرار الكبار التي باينت به أمثالها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r6.claim: Ḍabḥ is the loud breathing sound from horses' mouths during intense running, distinct from neighing, snorting, or a camel's bellow.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r6.anchor: والضبح صوت جهير من أفواهها عند العدو الشديد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas renders the horses' ḍabḥ as the sound ah ah, or as running short of a full gallop.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r7.anchor: وحكاه ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما فقال : أح أح , أو الضبح عدو دون التقريب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r8.claim: The sound was originally associated with foxes and then borrowed for horses; horses, dogs, and foxes are the animals said to make it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p508#2/r8.anchor: ليس من الدواب يضبح غير الفرس والكلب والثعلب

DURR-FULL:v8p599/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and has eleven verses.

DURR-FULL:v8p599/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the surah al-Adiyat was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت و العاديات بمكة

DURR-FULL:v8p599/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reports a Prophetic saying that both al-Zalzalah and al-Adiyat each equal half the Quran.
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r3.anchor: عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (إذا زلزلت)

DURR-FULL:v8p599/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r4.claim: A report through ʿAta ibn Abi Rabah from Ibn Abbas assigns half the Quran to al-Zalzalah and al-Adiyat, a third to al-Ikhlas, and a quarter to al-Kafirun.
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (إذا زلزلت) تعدل نصف القرآن

DURR-FULL:v8p599/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r5.claim: The Prophet sent cavalry away for a month without news, and the surah was revealed during their absence.
DURR-FULL:v8p599/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خيلا فاستمرت شهرا لا يأتيه منها خبر

DURR-FULL:v8p600/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r1.claim: The horses make a ḍabḥ with their feet; Ibn Mardawayh's wording instead says they snort through their nostrils.
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r1.anchor: ضحت بأرجلها ولفظ ابن مردويه ضبحت بمناخيرها

DURR-FULL:v8p600/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the episode as an expedition whose delayed report troubled the Prophet; God informed him of its progress and outcome.
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سرية إلى العدو فأبطأ خبرها فشق ذلك عليه

DURR-FULL:v8p600/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r7.claim: The horses' ḍabḥ is their snorting while racing.
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r7.anchor: قال: هي الخيل والضبح: نخير الخيل حتى تنخر

DURR-FULL:v8p600/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says the horses in battle lower their lips as they prepare to race, and that sparks expose the pagans' stratagem.
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس هي الخيل في القتال وضبحها حين ترخي مشافرها إذا أعدت

DURR-FULL:v8p600/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r14.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r14.claim: Abu Salih insists that Ali interpreted the oath as pilgrimage camels and says his own patron was more knowledgeable than Ikrima's.
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r14.anchor: قال أبو صالح: فقلت: قال علي: هي الإبل في الحج ومولاي كان أعلم من مولاك

DURR-FULL:v8p600/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r15.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r15.claim: Ali rejects the cavalry reading because early Badr had only the reported horses; he identifies the oath with pilgrims' camels running from Arafat through Muzdalifa, where they kindle fires.
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r15.anchor: والله إن أول غزوة في الإسلام لبدر وما كان معنا إلا فرسان للزبير وفرس للمقداد بن الأسود

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r1.claim: Asked about the oath, Ibn Abbas first says it means horses raiding for God and resting at night; Ali objects that Badr had only a few horses and says the camels run from Arafat to Muzdalifa and Mina, raising dust and reaching Jam. Ibn Abbas recants.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : فنزعت عن قولي ورجعت إلى الذي قال علي

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r2.claim: Abdullah (Ibn Masʿud) interprets the oath as camels.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله والعاديات ضبحا قال : الابل

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r3.claim: Ibrahim reports Ali's interpretation as camels and says Ibn Abbas connected the verse to a dispatched expedition.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r3.anchor: قال إبراهيم : وقال علي بن أبي طالب : هي الابل وقال ابن عباس : إنما كان ذلك في سرية بعثت

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says only dogs and horses among animals make a ḍabḥ.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس والعاديات ضبحا قال : ليس بشيء من الدواب يضبح الا كلب أو فرس

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r7.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r7.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr used to identify the oath animals as camels.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r7.anchor: عبيد بن عمير يقول : هي الإبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r1.claim: Early Qayrawan, Tunisian, and eastern codices and some commentaries call it al-Adiyat without waw; other tafsirs retain the opening waw in the title.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r1.anchor: سميت في المصاحف القيروانية العتيقة والتونسية والمشرقية ( سورة العاديات ) بدون واو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Jabir ibn Zayd, Ata, al-Hasan, and Ikrima classify the surah as Meccan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r2.anchor: فقال ابن مسعود وجابر بن زيد وعطاء والحسن وعكرمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r3.claim: Anas ibn Malik, Ibn Abbas, and Qatada classify the surah as Medinan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r3.anchor: وقال أنس بن مالك وابن عباس وقتادة : هي مدنية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r4.speaker: جابر بن زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r4.claim: On the Meccan classification, Jabir ibn Zayd ranks it fourteenth in revelation order, after al-Asr and before al-Kawthar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r4.anchor: وعدت الرابعة عشرة في ترتيب نزول السور عند جابر بن زيد بناء على أنها مكية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r6.claim: Al-Wahidi attributes to Muqatil and others a report that a cavalry force sent against Banu Kinana was delayed for a month, rumors said they had died, and the verses announced their deeds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r6.anchor: ذكر الواحدي في ( أسباب النزول ) عن مقاتل وعن غيره أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث خيلا سرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r7.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the Bazzar version of the expedition report very strange.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r7.anchor: وقال ابن كثير : روى أبو بكر البزار هنا حديثا غريبا جدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r8.claim: Despite its strangeness, the report could be accepted, but its chain contains the weak Hafs ibn Jamiʿ; the stronger view is that the surah is Medinan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r8.anchor: إلا أن في سنده حفص بن جميع وهو ضعيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r9.claim: The surah condemns traits leading to loss in the afterlife, especially prevalent among pagans and hypocrites, and warns Muslims against them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r9.anchor: ذم خصال تفضي بأصحابها إلى الخسران في الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r10.claim: It reminds people that their deeds will be judged after death, reassuring believers and threatening deniers; the opening oath also honors warhorses or pilgrimage mounts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p497/r10.anchor: ووعظ الناس بأن وراءهم حسابا على أعمالهم بعد الموت ليتذكره المؤمن ويهدد به الجاحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r1.claim: Al-Adiyat is the active participle of running quickly, used especially for horses and camels, and by analogy for renowned human runners.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r1.anchor: جمع العادية ، وهو اسم فاعل من العدو وهو السير السريع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r2.claim: Four Arab runners were proverbial: al-Sulayk ibn al-Salka, al-Shanfara, Taʾabbata Sharran, and Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r2.anchor: السليك بن السلكة ، والشنفرى ، وتأبط شرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r3.claim: The feminine form agrees with its non-rational referent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r3.anchor: وتأنيث هذا الوصف هنا لأنه من صفات ما لا يعقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r4.claim: Ḍabḥ is breath vibrating in the throat without leaving the mouth, a sound made by horses and predatory animals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r4.anchor: والضبح : اضطراب النفس المتردد في الحنجرة دون أن يخرج من الفم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas demonstrates ḍabḥ by imitating the sound ah ah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r5.anchor: وعن عطاء : سمعت ابن عباس يصف الضبح أح أح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says no animal besides a horse, dog, or fox makes a ḍabḥ; the lexicographers also report this view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ليس شيء من الدواب يضبح غير الفرس والكلب والثعلب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas first identified the oath with horses raiding for God; Ali argued Badr had only two horses and instead identified pilgrimage camels traveling from Arafat to Muzdalifa and Mina, so Ibn Abbas withdrew his answer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس : فنزعت عن قولي ورجعت إلى الذي قال علي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r8.claim: Ali's words do not explicitly classify the surah as Meccan or Medinan; Ibn Masʿud, Ibrahim, Mujahid, and Ubayd ibn Umayr give the same camel interpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p498/r8.anchor: وليس في قول علي رضي الله عنه تصريح بأنها مكية ولا مدنية وبمثل ما قال علي قال ابن مسعود وإبراهيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r1.claim: Linguists do not use ḍabḥ for camel sounds; on a camel reading, al-Mubarrad and others interpret it as ḍabʿ, extending the forelegs while running.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r1.anchor: والضبح لا يطلق على صوت الإبل في قول أهل اللغة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda says horses may also be described by the related verb for extending their forelegs when running, with ḍabḥ a dialect form replacing ʿayn with ḥaʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : ضبحت الخيل وضبعت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r3.speaker: الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r3.claim: Al-Kashshaf rejects the proposed letter interchange as unsupported, though al-Qamus adopts it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r4.claim: With camels, ḍabḥ can be a metaphor for their intensified running sound, or a dialectal substitution for ḍabʿ.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r5.claim: Ḍabḥan may be an accusative circumstantial expression of their sound, or describe the manner of running if derived from ḍabʿ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r5.anchor: إذا أريد به الصوت الذي يتردد في جوفها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r6.claim: If the oath concerns pilgrimage camels, it honors animals whose service is esteemed by both pagans and Muslims, making the sworn claim persuasive to all.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p499/r6.anchor: واختير القسم بها لأن السامعين يوقنون أن ما يقسم عليه بها محقق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p500/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p500/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p500/r9.claim: The carefully chosen words accommodate both warhorses and pilgrimage camels, a feature of the surah's rhetorical arrangement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p500/r9.anchor: ومن بديع النظم وإعجازه إيثار كلمات ( العاديات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Mujahid, and Ikrima identify the oath animals as horses running with their riders and making a sound; an expedition to Banu Kinana may have occasioned the surah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد وعكرمة: أراد الخيل لأنها تعدو بالفرسان وتصيح بأصواتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r2.claim: Another view takes the oath as horses generally, whose speed and strength have long made them conquer lands and kingdoms; good remains in their forelocks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: القسم هو بالخيل جملة لأنها تعدو ضابحة قديما وحديثا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r3.claim: Ali, Ibn Masʿud, Ibrahim, and Ubayd ibn Umayr say the animals are camels, which make a ḍabḥ while running; Ali includes pilgrims' and Badr's camels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r3.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب وابن مسعود وإبراهيم وعبيد بن عمير: العاديات في هذه الآية: الإبل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r4.claim: Ali says the oath refers to pilgrims' camels running between Arafat and Muzdalifa, as well as Badr's camels, since that battle had very few horses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r4.anchor: قال علي: والقسم بالإبل العاديات من عرفة ومن مزدلفة إذا وقع الحاج وبإبل غزوة بدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r5.claim: Ḍabḥ is a loud sound during intense running, distinct from neighing, roaring, and barking; it is an unusual animal sound.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r5.anchor: والضبح: تصويت جهير عند العدو الشديد ليس بصهيل ولا رغاء ولا نباح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to say that only horses and dogs make a ḍabḥ; the author rejects this as unsound because Arabs also apply the word to camels, snakes, owls, rabbits, foxes, echoes, and bows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r6.anchor: وحكي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أنه قال: ليس يضبح من الحيوان غير الخيل والكلاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa's verse about a bow making a fox-like ḍabḥ in the hand supports the word's broader use beyond horses and dogs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r7.anchor: وأنشد أبو حنيفة في صفة قوس: [الرجز] حنانة من نشم أو تالب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r8.claim: The oath may concern warhorses, pilgrimage camels, or both.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p513#2/r8.anchor: والظاهر في الآية، أن القسم بالخيل أو بالإبل أو بهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r1.speaker: علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r1.claim: One view identifies the oath as pilgrimage camels, held by Ali, Ibn Masʿud, Ubayd ibn Umayr, al-Qurazi, and al-Suddi; Ali says they run from Arafat through Muzdalifa to Mina.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنها الإبل في الحج قاله علي وابن مسعود وعبيد بن عمير والقرظي والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r2.speaker: علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r2.claim: A report from Ali describes Badr, saying the Muslims then had only one horse, though another report gives two.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r2.anchor: وروي عن علي أنه قال هذا في صفة وقعة بدر قال وما كان معنا يومئذ إلا فرس وفي بعض الحديث أنه كان معهم فرسان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r3.claim: The other view identifies the oath as horses campaigning for God; it is attributed to Ibn Abbas, Hasan, Ata, Mujahid, and other early authorities and linguists.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r3.anchor: والثاني أنها الخيل في سبيل الله قاله ابن عباس والحسن وعطاء ومجاهد وأبو العالية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas understood the horses to be from an expedition sent by the Prophet whose news was delayed for a month.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r4.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يذهب إلى أن هذا كان في سرية فروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله بعث خيلا فلم يأته خبرها شهرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r5.claim: In the expedition account, the horses snort through their nostrils, spark with their hooves on stones, attack at dawn, raise dust, and reach the enemy together.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r5.anchor: ضبحت بمناخرها فالموريات قدحا قدحت بحوافرها الحجارة فأورت نارا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r6.claim: Muqatil says a force sent to two Banu Kinana clans under al-Mundhir ibn Amr was delayed; rumors by Jews and hypocrites made Muslims fear their relatives had died.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سرية إلى حيين من كنانة واستعمل عليها المنذر بن عمرو الأنصاري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r7.claim: The surah was revealed to report how the expedition had fared and to allay the fear stirred by the rumors.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r7.anchor: فنزلت والعاديات ضبحا فأخبر الله كيف فعل بهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r8.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r8.claim: Al-Farra defines ḍabḥ as the sound of horses' breaths when they run.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r8.anchor: قال الفراء الضبح أصوات أنفاس الخيل إذا عدون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r9.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba says ḍabḥ is the sound in horses' throats when they run.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة الضبح صوت حلوقها إذا عدت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj says ḍabḥ is the sound of the horses' insides when they run.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r10.anchor: وقال الزجاج ضبحها صوت أجوافها إذا عدت

IBNKATHIR:100:1/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:100:1/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:100:1/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir classifies al-ʿĀdiyāt as Meccan.

IBNKATHIR:100:1/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:100:1/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:100:1/r2.claim: God swears by horses running in His cause; ḍabḥ is the sound of their breath as they run.
IBNKATHIR:100:1/r2.anchor: يقسم تعالى بالخيل إذا أجريت في سبيله فَعَدت وضَبَحت

JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وقتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.claim: Al-Hasan, ʿIkrimah, and Qatadah say the surah is Meccan; another view says it is Medinan and was revealed around a raid.
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.anchor: قيل: إنها مكية، عن الحسن، وعكرمة، وقتادة. وقيل: مدنية، وقالوا: نزلت عند جهاد وقع في سرية.

JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for reciting the surah for every person who spent the night at Muzdalifah and witnessed Jamʿ.
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.anchor: من قرأ سورة (والعاديات) أعطي من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد من بات بالمزدلفة وشهد جمعا

JISHUMI:v10p7511/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r8.claim: Al-ʿādiyāt is the plural of ʿādiyah.

JISHUMI:v10p7511/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r9.claim: Ḍabḥ may be horses’ snorting while running, their heavy breathing, or more generally a sound; lexicographers also compare it to ḍabaʿ, running with full extension of the forelegs.
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r9.anchor: والضبح الضبع، وهو أن يمد ضبعيه حتى لا يجد مزيدا

JISHUMI:v10p7511/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r10.claim: The passage also says animals pant when changed by exhaustion, fear, or desire; horses, dogs, and foxes are named as animals that pant.
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r10.anchor: وإنما تضبح هذه الحيوانات إذا تغيرت حالها من تعب أو فزع أو طمع.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r1.claim: The oath is by war horses running and panting; ḍabḥ is the sound of their breathing, which Ibn Abbas imitated as “aḥ aḥ.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r1.anchor: أقسم بخيل الغزاة تعدو فتضبح . والضبح : صوت أنفاسها إذا عدون . وعن ابن عباس أنه حكاه فقال : أح أح .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r2.speaker: عنترة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r2.claim: Antarah’s line depicts horses panting as they struggle in the pools of death, serving as poetic evidence for ḍabḥ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r2.anchor: والخيل تكدح حين تض بح في حياض الموت ضبحا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r3.claim: Ḍabḥan can be a cognate accusative of an implied verb, modify the horses as “panting,” or function as a circumstantial accusative.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r3.anchor: وانتصاب ضبحا على : يضبحن ضبحا ، أو بالعاديات ، كأنه قيل : والضابحات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r11.claim: A questioner repeated Ibn Abbas’s horse interpretation to Ali, who rebuked him: at Badr the Muslims had only two horses.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r11.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ( 1334 ) كنت جالسا في الحجر فجاء رجل فسألني عن { والعاديات ضبحا } ففسرتها بالخيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r12.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r12.claim: Ali argues that Badr had only two horses, one belonging to al-Zubayr and one to al-Miqdad, and interprets the oath as pilgrimage camels traveling between the rites.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r12.anchor: والله إن كانت لأول غزوة في الإسلام بدر ، وما كان معنا إلا فرسان : فرس الزبير وفرس للمقداد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r13.claim: If the report is sound, applying ḍabḥ to camels is a metaphor, like borrowing animal terms for human or other bodies; another view restricts ḍabḥ to horses, dogs, and foxes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r13.anchor: فإن صحت الرواية فقد استعير الضبح للإبل ، كما استعير المشافر والحافر للإنسان ، والشفتان للمهر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r14.claim: A further, expressly insecure explanation equates ḍabḥ with ḍabʿ, the camel’s stretching of its forelegs while moving.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r14.anchor: وقيل : الضبح بمعنى الضبع ، يقال : ضبحت الإبل وضبعت : إذا مدت أضباعها في السير ، وليس بثبت .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for reciting al-ʿĀdiyāt for every person who spent the night at Muzdalifah and witnessed Jamʿ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.anchor: ( 1335 ) ( من قرأ سورة والعاديات أعطي من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد من بات بالمزدلفة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وأنس والحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r1.claim: They interpret al-ʿādiyāt as horses used in jihad, supported by a cited line about a horse at the charge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r1.anchor: في العاديات قولان : أحدهما : أنها الخيل في الجهاد , قاله ابن عباس وأنس والحسن , ومنه قول الشاعر :

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r2.speaker: علي وابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r2.claim: They interpret al-ʿādiyāt as camels during pilgrimage, supported by Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib’s verse about the animals at Jamʿ.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنها الإبل في الحج , قاله علي رضي الله عنه وابن مسعود ومنه قول صفية بنت عبد المطلب :

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r3.claim: Under the horse view, ḍabḥ is snorting while running; under the camel view, it is labored breathing during fast travel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r3.anchor: وفي قوله ( ضبحا ) وجهان : أحدهما : أن الضبح حمحمة الخيل عند العدو

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas describes camel ḍabḥ as the driver’s call, aj aj.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.claim: The following Sūrat al-Qāriʿah is Meccan according to all the authorities mentioned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.anchor: سورة القارعة مكية في قولهم جميعا

MUJAHID:v2p776/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p776/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p776/r1.claim: Mujahid explains al-ʿādiyāt as horses that pant while running.
MUJAHID:v2p776/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ والعاديات ضبحا ﴾ يعني الخيل تضبح

MUQATIL:100:1-6/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r1.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r1.claim: One occasion report says Muhammad sent a Kinana expedition to Hunayn under al-Mundhir ibn Amr; when it sent no news, God informed him about it through the oath by the horses.
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r1.anchor: ذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث سرية إلى حنين من كنانة، واستعمل عليهم المنذر بن عمرو الأنصاري

MUQATIL:100:1-6/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r2.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r2.claim: An alternative says an expedition to Tihamah was late; Jewish and hypocritical onlookers caused anxiety about missing relatives, then Gabriel came Friday morning to explain that the horses had charged until they panted like foxes.
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r2.anchor: وقيل: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث سرية إلى أرض تهامة، وأبطأ عليه الخبر، فجعلت اليهود والمنافقون

NASAFI-FULL:v4p353/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353/r1.claim: The oath is by war horses running and panting; their ḍabḥ is their breath-sound, which Ibn Abbas imitated as “aḥ aḥ.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353/r1.anchor: ﴿ والعاديات ضبحا ﴾ أقسم بخيل الغزاة تعدو فتضبح والضبح صوت أنفاسها إذا عدن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p353/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353/r2.claim: Ḍabḥan is an accusative governed by the implied verb they pant.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r1.speaker: جمهور المفسرين وأهل اللغة
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r1.claim: Most commentators and linguists say the oath is by horses running in God’s cause; Qatadah calls ḍabḥ their snorting, and al-Farra their breathing.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { والعاديات ضبحا } أي الأفراس تعدو. كذا قال عامة المفسرين وأهل اللغة أي تعدو في سبيل الله
