QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says only horses, dogs, and foxes make the sound called ḍabḥ.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r2.anchor: ابن عباس: ليس شيء من الدواب يضبح غير الفرس والكلب والثعلب.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r3.claim: A proposed reason the horses breathe forcefully is that they were muzzled to prevent neighing from alerting the enemy.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r3.anchor: وقيل: كانت تكعم لئلا تصهل، فيعلم العدو بهم فكانت تتنفس في هذه الحال بقوة.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r4.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says God swears by Muhammad in Yā Sīn, by Muhammad’s life in al-Ḥijr, and here by his cavalry, its neighing, dust, and sparks.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r4.anchor: قال ابن العربي: أقسم الله بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r5.speaker: أهل اللغة
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r5.claim: Linguists cite poetry describing horses at the charge as evidence for the horse interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r5.anchor: وقال أهل اللغة: وطعنة ذات رشاش واهيه طعنتها عند صدور العاديه يعني الخيل.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r6.speaker: عنترة
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r6.claim: Antarah’s verse describes horses panting in the pools of death, illustrating ḍabḥ.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r6.anchor: وقال عنترة: والخيل تعلم حين تض بح في حياض الموت ضبحا

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r7.claim: The word originally describes foxes and was transferred metaphorically to horses; it is related to fire changing a color without fully consuming it.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r7.anchor: وأصل الضبح والضباح للثعالب فاستعير للخيل. وهو من قول العرب: ضبحته النار: إذا غيرت لونه ولم تبالغ فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r8.claim: The horses and other named animals pant when fatigue, fear, or desire changes their condition.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r8.anchor: وإنما تضبح هذه الحيوانات إذا تغيرت حالها من فزع وتعب أو طمع.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r9.claim: Ḍabḥan is a cognate accusative for the horses’ panting; Basrans also analyze it as a circumstantial accusative or verbal noun used circumstantially.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r9.anchor: ونصب «ضبحا» على المصدر أي والعاديات تضبح ضبحا.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r10.claim: Abu Ubaydah compares ḍabḥ to ḍabʿ, meaning movement or running; al-Mubarrad explains the latter as extending the forelegs while moving.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r10.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: ضبحت الخيل ضبحا مثل ضبعت وهو السير.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r12.claim: A report says a company sent to Banu Kinana under al-Mundhir ibn Amr was delayed; the surah reassured Muhammad that it was safe and had raided its target.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r12.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث سرية إلى أناس من بني كنانة، فأبطأ عليه خبرها

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r13.claim: The report identifies al-Mundhir ibn Amr, one of the leaders at al-Aqabah, as the commander of the expedition.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2/r13.anchor: وكان استعمل عليهم المنذر بن عمرو الأنصاري، وكان أحد النقباء فقال المنافقون: إنهم قتلوا

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r1.claim: A transmitted saying calls failure to recognize the sanctity of a warrior’s horse a branch of hypocrisy.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r1.anchor: " من لم يعرف حرمة فرس الغازي، ففيه شعبة من النفاق "

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r2.speaker: مسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r2.claim: Muslim reports disputing Ikrimah’s horse interpretation with Ali’s view that the oath concerns pilgrimage camels; he says his own master Ali is more knowledgeable.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r2.anchor: قال مسلم: نازعت فيها عكرمة فقال عكرمة: قال ابن عباس هي الخيل. وقلت: قال علي هي الإبل في الحج، ومولاي أعلم من مولاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r3.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says Ali and Ibn Abbas disputed the verse: Ali identified camels running for pilgrimage, while Ibn Abbas identified horses.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r3.anchor: وقال الشعبي: تمارى علي وابن عباس في «العاديات»، فقال علي: هي الإبل تعدو في الحج. وقال ابن عباس: هي الخيل

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r4.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r4.claim: Ali counters that Badr, the first Islamic battle, had only two horses, and concludes that al-ʿādiyāt are camels traveling from Arafah to Muzdalifah and Mina.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r4.anchor: والله إن كانت لأول غزوة في الإسلام وما معنا إلا فرسان: فرس للمقداد، وفرس للزبير

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to have returned to Ali’s camel interpretation; Ibn Masud, Ubayd ibn Umayr, Muhammad ibn Kab, and al-Suddi also hold it.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فرجعت إلى قول علي، وبه قال ابن مسعود وعبيد بن عمير ومحمد بن كعب والسدي.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r6.speaker: صفية بنت عبد المطلب
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r6.claim: Safiyyah’s poem refers to camels at Jamʿ raising dust, as evidence for the pilgrimage interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r6.anchor: ومنه قول صفية بنت عبد المطلب: فلا والعاديات غداة جمع بأيديها إذا سطع الغبار

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r7.claim: Al-ʿādiyāt derives from running, meaning rapid movement with the legs spread apart.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r7.anchor: وسميت العاديات لاشتقاقها من العدو، وهو تباعد الأرجل في سرعة المشي.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r8.claim: For the camel view, ḍabḥ is taken as ḍabʿ by substituting ḥāʾ for ʿayn; ḍabʿ refers to extending the forelegs during travel.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r8.anchor: ومن قال هي الإبل فقوله «ضبحا» بمعنى ضبعا فالحاء عنده مبدلة من العين

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r9.speaker: أبو صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r9.claim: Abu Salih says horses make ḍabḥ by snorting, while camels do so by breathing.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r9.anchor: الضبح من الخيل: الحمحمة، ومن الإبل التنفس.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r10.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r10.claim: Ata says only horses, foxes, and dogs make the sound called ḍabḥ.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r10.anchor: قال عطاء: ليس شيء من الدواب يضبح إلا الفرس والثعلب والكلب

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r11.speaker: توبة
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r11.claim: Tawbah’s poem describes a fox crying out from a graveyard, showing that ḍabḥ can describe a fox’s cry.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#2/r11.anchor: قال توبة: ولو أن ليلى الأخيلية سلمت علي ودوني تربة وصفائح

QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#3/r3.claim: A report from Mujahid says Ibn Abbas applied the verses both to battle and to pilgrimage.
QURTUBI-FULL:100:1-2#3/r3.anchor: روى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد { والعاديات ضبحا * فالموريات قدحا } قال: قال ابن عباس: هو في القتال وهو في الحج.

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.claim: The Meccan surah has eleven verses and moves in rapid, forceful jumps before settling at its ending, like a runner reaching the finish.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.anchor: سورة العاديات مكية وآياتها إحدى عشرة يجري سياق هذه السورة في لمسات سريعة عنيفة مثيرة

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r2.claim: The opening scene shows charging, panting horses striking sparks, attacking at dawn, raising dust, and suddenly breaking into enemy ranks.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r2.anchor: وتبدأ بمشهد الخيل العادية الضابحة ، القادحة للشرر بحوافرها ، المغيرة مع الصباح

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.claim: The rough, rumbling, cracking rhythm suits the noisy dust and forceful disclosure of graves and hearts, as well as the surah’s ingratitude and greed.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.anchor: والإيقاع الموسيقي فيه خشونة ودمدمة وفرقعة ، تناسب الجو الصاخب المعفر

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r7.claim: The oath’s noisy cavalry scene frames the surah’s moral and resurrection scenes: image and frame mirror one another.
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r7.anchor: فكان الإطار من الصورة والصورة من الإطار

RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r1.claim: Ḍabḥ is the sound of horses’ breath while running, neither neighing nor whinnying.
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن الضبح أصوات أنفاس الخيل إذا عدت ، وهو صوت ليس بصهيل ولا حمحمة

RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r2.speaker: علي وابن مسعود وإبراهيم والقرظي
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r2.claim: They interpret al-ʿādiyāt as pilgrimage camels; the report from Ibn Abbas says Ali rebuked his earlier horse interpretation because Badr had only two horses.
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r2.anchor: الأول : ما روى عن علي عليه السلام وابن مسعود أنها الإبل ، وهو قول إبراهيم والقرظي

RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r3.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r3.claim: Ali’s interpretation has the camels travel from Arafah to Muzdalifah and then Mina; Ibn Abbas is said to have retracted his first answer.
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r3.anchor: الإبل من عرفة إلى مزدلفة ، ومن المزدلفة إلى منى ، يعني إبل الحاج ، قال ابن عباس : فرجعت عن قولي إلى قول علي

RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r8.claim: The oath may recall the many benefits of camels cited in 88:17, contrast human rebellion with God’s service to people, or encourage pilgrimage; neglecting required Hajj is characterized as disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r8.anchor: فوجه القسم به من وجوه أحدها : ما ذكرنا من المنافع الكثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r9.speaker: أبي عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r9.claim: A report attributed to Ubay and raised to the Prophet promises a reward measured by the number who spend a night at Muzdalifah and witness Jamʿ.
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r9.anchor: ويتأكد هذا القول بما روى أبي في فضل السورة مرفوعا : ( من قرأها أعطى من الأجر

RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك وعطاء
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ata, and most careful exegetes say al-ʿādiyāt are horses; a report also attributes this reading to the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r1.anchor: القول الثاني : قول ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك وعطاء وأكثر المحققين : أنه الخيل ، وروى ذلك مرفوعا

RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r2.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the oath followed a delayed report from an expedition sent against some of Kinana, which worried Muhammad until Gabriel informed him of its progress.
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي : بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سرية إلى أناس من كنانة فمكث ما شاء الله أن يمكث لا يأتيه منهم خبر

RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r3.claim: The definite article may refer to the particular expedition’s horses, or generically to all horses that run in God’s cause.
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r3.anchor: فإن جعلنا الألف واللام في : { والعاديات } للمعهود السابق كان محل القسم خيل تلك السرية

RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r4.claim: Al-Razi prefers horses: ḍabḥ properly belongs to horses, sparks suit iron horseshoes better than camel feet, and dawn attacks are easier on horseback; borrowing for camels is unnecessary metaphor.
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r4.anchor: وذلك لأن الضبح لا يكون إلا للفرس ، واستعمال هذا اللفظ في الإبل يكون على سبيل الاستعارة

RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r5.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says that if the horse view is accepted, the surah is most likely Medinan because permission to fight came in Medina.
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r5.anchor: فالأقرب أن السورة مدنية ، لأن الإذن بالقتال كان بالمدينة ، وهو الذي قاله الكلبي

RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r6.claim: Horses serve pursuit, escape, attack, and retreat; the oath recognizes their worldly and religious benefits and warns against keeping them only for display.
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r6.anchor: أقسم بالخيل لأن لها في العدو من الخصال الحميدة ما ليس لسائر الدواب ، فإنها تصلح للطلب والهرب والكر والفر

RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r7.claim: The verse about horses, mules, and donkeys says they are for riding and adornment, but its purpose marker applies to riding, not ornament.
RAZI-FULL:v32p61/r7.anchor: في قوله : { والخيل والبغال والحمير لتركبوها وزينة } فأدخل لام التعليل على الركوب

RAZI-FULL:v32p61#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p61#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v32p61#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj treats ḍabḥan as a cognate accusative governed by the implied verb the horses pant.

RAZI-FULL:v32p61#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p61#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v32p61#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra parses al-ʿādiyāt as al-ḍābiḥāt, since panting accompanies running.
RAZI-FULL:v32p61#2/r2.anchor: أن يكون { والعاديات } في معنى والضابحات ، لأن الضبح يكون مع العدو

RAZI-FULL:v32p61#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p61#2/r3.speaker: البصريون
RAZI-FULL:v32p61#2/r3.claim: The Basrans analyze ḍabḥan as a circumstantial accusative, meaning panting.
RAZI-FULL:v32p61#2/r3.anchor: قال البصريون : التقدير : والعاديات ضابحة ، فقوله : { ضبحا } نصب على الحال

STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r1.claim: Most commentators date the surah early Makkan, likely after al-Qāriʿah; others place it early Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r1.anchor: ost commentators maintain that al-ʿĀdiyāt was revealed

STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r2.claim: The Makkan attribution draws on stylistic similarity; the Madinan view draws on some interpretations of the subject.
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r2.anchor: The case for Makkan attribution is supported by its similarity in style

STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r3.claim: One occasion report describes al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr's expedition to Banū Kinānah: after news was delayed and hypocrites said the men had been killed, the verse announced its horses.
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r3.anchor: In the first, it is reported that the Prophet sent a military expedition

STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r4.claim: Others connect the verses to Badr; a report attributed to ʿAlī says only two horses were there and the other mounts were camels.
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r4.anchor: Others have said that the verses refer to the Battle of Badr, but according to an account attributed to ʿAlī

STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r5.speaker: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r5.claim: Another account attributed to ʿAlī sees the oaths as pilgrims rushing from ʿArafāt to Muzdalifah and Minā.
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r5.anchor: Another account attributed to ʿAlī sees these oaths as depictions of that portion

STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r6.claim: The first five verses swear by chargers; 6–8 discuss human ingratitude, while 9–11 warn of judgment and disclosure of hearts.
STUDYQURAN:100:intro/r6.anchor: The sūrah begins with five oaths by various forms of charging horses

STUDYQURAN:100:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:100:1/r1.speaker: al-Bayḍāwī
STUDYQURAN:100:1/r1.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī allegorizes the chargers as souls transmitting holiness, kindling spiritual knowledge, attacking caprice, raising desire for God, and entering the highest Garden.
STUDYQURAN:100:1/r1.anchor: According to al-Bayḍāwī, the oaths in these verses can also be seen as

STUDYQURAN:100:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:100:1/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:100:1/r2.claim: The oaths can refer to battle horses or pilgrimage camels, and to both since each performs a function worthy of God's oath.
STUDYQURAN:100:1/r2.anchor: it can be seen as applying to both, as each is understood as fulfilling a function

TABATABAI:100:1-5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r1.claim: The surah recalls human ingratitude and love of wealth, known to people and evidence against them at judgment.
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r1.anchor: بيان تذكر السورة كفران الإنسان لنعم ربه وحبه الشديد للخير

TABATABAI:100:1-5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r2.claim: The surah is Madinan because its oaths appear to describe warrior horses and jihad began after the Hijra.
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r2.anchor: والسورة مدنية بشهادة ما في صدرها من الإقسام

TABATABAI:100:1-5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r3.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r3.claim: Shiite reports from the Imams say it concerns ʿAlī and Dhāt al-Salāsil; some Sunni reports support this.
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r3.anchor: أن السورة نزلت في علي عليه السلام وسريته في غزوة ذات السلاسل

TABATABAI:100:1-5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r4.claim: Al-ʿĀdiyāt is fast running; dabḥ is the familiar sound of horses' breath, and the following descriptions favor horses.
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r4.anchor: العاديات من العدو وهو الجري بسرعة والضبح صوت أنفاس الخيل

TABATABAI:100:1-5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r5.claim: Alternatives identify pilgrims' camels or camels in a raid; later descriptions do not fit the camel reading.
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد بها إبل الحاج في ارتفاعها بركبانها من الجمع إلى منى

TABATABAI:100:1-5/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r13.claim: The apparent meanings of all five verses favor cavalry on a particular raid, whose successive actions are linked by the fāʾs.
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r13.anchor: فالمتعين حملها على خيل الغزاة وسياق الآيات وخاصة قوله

TABATABAI:100:1-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:1-11/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:100:1-11/r1.claim: A report from Abū ʿAbd Allāh says Dhāt al-Salāsil was named for captives bound in ropes like chains.
TABATABAI:100:1-11/r1.anchor: وهو المروي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث طويل. قال وسميت هذه الغزوة ذات السلاسل

TABATABAI:100:1-11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:1-11/r2.speaker: the Prophet
TABATABAI:100:1-11/r2.claim: The Prophet recited the surah at dawn and said Gabriel announced ʿAlī's victory; ʿAlī later returned with captives and spoils.
TABATABAI:100:1-11/r2.anchor: نعم إن عليا ظفر بأعداء الله وبشرني بذلك جبريل في هذه الليلة

TABRISI:100:1/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:100:1/r5.claim: Dabḥ is horses' panting or strained breath; another view equates it to dabʿ, extending the foreleg in fast travel.
TABRISI:100:1/r5.anchor: الضبح في الخيل الحمحمة عند العدو. وقيل: هو شدة النفس

TABRISI:100:1/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1/r12.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:100:1/r12.claim: Muqātil says the delayed Kinanah expedition under al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr prompted the revelation announcing its horses after hypocrites said the men were killed.
TABRISI:100:1/r12.anchor: قتلوا جميعا فأخبر الله تعالى عنها بقوله { والعاديات ضبحا } عن مقاتل.

TABRISI:100:1/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1/r13.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:100:1/r13.claim: A report from Abū ʿAbd Allāh connects the surah with ʿAlī's campaign at Dhāt al-Salāsil after prior commanders had returned.
TABRISI:100:1/r13.anchor: المروي عن أبي عبد الله ع في حديث طويل قال وسميت هذه الغزوة ذات السلاسل

TABRISI:100:1-4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1-4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:100:1-4/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and several Successors identify the chargers as horses running against unbelievers.
TABRISI:100:1-4/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس وعطاء وعكرمة والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة والربيع قالوا أقسم الله بالخيل العادية

TABRISI:100:1-4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1-4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:100:1-4/r2.claim: For the horse view, dabḥ is their breath while running, not neighing or whinnying.
TABRISI:100:1-4/r2.anchor: وضبحها صوت أجوافها إذا عدت ليس بصهيل ولا حمحمة ولكنه صوت نفس

TABRISI:100:1-4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1-4/r3.speaker: علي
TABRISI:100:1-4/r3.claim: ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, and al-Suddī identify the chargers as camels, including pilgrims' camels going from ʿArafāt to Muzdalifah and Minā.
TABRISI:100:1-4/r3.anchor: روي ذلك عن علي ع وابن مسعود والسدي

TABRISI:100:1-4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1-4/r4.speaker: صفية بنت عبد المطلب
TABRISI:100:1-4/r4.claim: Ṣafiyyah's poem pictures chargers at Jamʿ with dust rising, supporting the camel view.
TABRISI:100:1-4/r4.anchor: قالت صفية بنت عبد المطلب: ألا والعاديات غداة جمع

TABRISI:100:1-4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1-4/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
TABRISI:100:1-4/r5.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says ʿAlī's view is more authoritative than Ibn ʿAbbās's because his master knows better.
TABRISI:100:1-4/r5.anchor: فقلت أنا قال علي ع: هي الإبل في الحج وقلت مولاي أعلم من مولاك

TABRISI:100:1-4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1-4/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:100:1-4/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās argues horses raise dust with their hooves and pant; ʿAlī replies Badr had only two horses.
TABRISI:100:1-4/r6.anchor: فهل تثيره إلا بحوافرها وهل تضبح الإبل إنما تضبح الخيل

TABRISI:100:1-4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1-4/r7.speaker: علي
TABRISI:100:1-4/r7.claim: In the report from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAlī rebukes Ibn ʿAbbās, says the chargers are pilgrimage camels, and Ibn ʿAbbās retracts.
TABRISI:100:1-4/r7.anchor: ذهب إلى علي بن أبي طالب ع وهو تحت سقاية زمزم فسأله عن العاديات ضبحا

THALABI:v10p268#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p268#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p268#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and a list of Successors identify the chargers as horses running in God's cause.
THALABI:v10p268#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وعطاء ومجاهد وعكرمة والحسن والكلبي وأبو العالية

THALABI:v10p268#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p268#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p268#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says only horse, dog, and fox make dabḥ.
THALABI:v10p268#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ليس شيء من الدواب يضج غير الفرس والكلب والثعلب

THALABI:v10p268#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p268#3/r3.speaker: أهل اللغة
THALABI:v10p268#3/r3.claim: Lexicographers say dabḥ originally described foxes and extended to horses; animals pant from fatigue, fear, or appetite.
THALABI:v10p268#3/r3.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: أصل الضبح والضباح للثعالب فاستعير في الخيل

THALABI:v10p268#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p268#3/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p268#3/r4.claim: Dabḥan is a cognate accusative: the chargers pant.
THALABI:v10p268#3/r4.anchor: ونصب قوله: ضبحا على المصدر ومجازه: والعاديات تضبح ضبحا

THALABI:v10p268#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p268#3/r5.speaker: شاعر
THALABI:v10p268#3/r5.claim: An unnamed poet uses taḍbaḥ to describe horses in Iraq as lexical evidence.

THALABI:v10p268#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p268#3/r6.speaker: شاعر
THALABI:v10p268#3/r6.claim: A second poet describes blood-soaked chargers with necks like sacrificial stones.
THALABI:v10p268#3/r6.anchor: وقال آخر: والعاديات أسابي الدماء بها

THALABI:v10p268#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p268#3/r7.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v10p268#3/r7.claim: Muqātil says the delayed Kinanah expedition under al-Mundhir prompted the revelation announcing its horses after hypocrites said the men were killed.
THALABI:v10p268#3/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل: بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سرية إلى حي من كنانة

THALABI:v10p268#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p268#3/r8.speaker: الحكماء
THALABI:v10p268#3/r8.claim: Some authorities describe dabḥ as a rattling sound in the saddlebag; another says the horses' lips move as they run.
THALABI:v10p268#3/r8.anchor: وقال الحكماء: هو تقلقل الجرذان في القنب. وقيل: هو صوت إرخاء مشافرها

THALABI:v10p268#3/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p268#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p268#3/r9.claim: Abū al-Ḍuḥā says Ibn ʿAbbās described the panting as ‘aj aj.’
THALABI:v10p268#3/r9.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول: ضباحها أج أج

THALABI:v10p268#3/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p268#3/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p268#3/r10.claim: Another group identifies the chargers as camels.

THALABI:v10p268#3/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p268#3/r11.speaker: أبو صالح
THALABI:v10p268#3/r11.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ invokes ʿAlī's camel view over Ibn ʿAbbās's horse interpretation.
THALABI:v10p268#3/r11.anchor: فقلت أنا: (قال علي: هي الإبل في الحج)

THALABI:v10p268#3/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p268#3/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p268#3/r12.claim: Al-Shaʿbī recounts Ibn ʿAbbās arguing horses raise dust and pant; ʿAlī replies Badr had just the dapple horse of al-Miqdād.
THALABI:v10p268#3/r12.anchor: وقال الشعبي تمارى علي ابن عباس في قوله: والعاديات ضبحا فقال ابن عباس: هي الخيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and several Successors identify the chargers as horses in raids; al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj select this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هي الخيل في الغزو (¬2)، وهو قول عطاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says dabḥ is the sound of horses' breath while running.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: والضبح: أصوات أنفاس الخيل إذا عدون (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq says dabḥ is the sound from horses' insides as they run.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: معناه: والعاديات تضبح ضبحا، وهو صوت (أجوافها إذا عدت)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r4.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r4.claim: Al-Layth says the horses' audible sound is breath, not neighing or whinnying.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r4.anchor: وقال الليث: الخيل العاديات تضبح في عدوها ضبحا، وهو صوت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r5.claim: On the horse reading, the oath applies generally to horses running in God's cause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r5.anchor: وعلى هذا القول القسم عام بالخيل العادية في سبيل الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r6.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r6.claim: Al-Kalbī reports a delayed Kinanah expedition led by al-Mundhir, whose route Gabriel disclosed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r7.claim: Muqātil gives a similar expedition account and explains dabḥ as the horses' exerted breath.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r7.anchor: ونحو هذا قال مقاتل (¬1): وقالا (¬2) في قوله: "ضبحا" هو أنفاسها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r8.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r8.claim: ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, and Abū Ṣāliḥ say the chargers are pilgrims' camels from ʿArafāt through Muzdalifah to Minā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r8.anchor: وقال علي -رضي الله عنه-: {والعاديات ضبحا} الإبل في الحج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r9.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r9.claim: Al-Azharī takes camel dabḥ as dabʿ, stretching the forelegs; Abū ʿUbaydah treats the two words as equivalent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p235#2/r9.anchor: قال الأزهري: من جعلها الإبل جعل "ضبحا" بمعنى ضبعا

WAHIDI-QT:100:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:100:1/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:100:1/r1.claim: The chargers are horses in battle, panting with the sound of their insides while running.
WAHIDI-QT:100:1/r1.anchor: { والعاديات } يعني الخيل في الغزو { ضبحا } تضبح ضبحا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:100:1-8/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:100:1-8/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:100:1-8/r1.claim: The chargers are horses on raids; dabḥ is the sound of their insides as they run.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:100:1-8/r1.anchor: { والعاديات } يعني: الخيل في الغزو { ضبحا } تضبح ضبحا

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r1.claim: The initial wāw is an oath; al-ʿādiyāt is the feminine sound plural active participle of ʿadw, meaning to run or race quickly.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r1.anchor: Vâv kasemdir. “Âdiyat” hızla koşmak, seğirtmek mânasına “adv”den ism-i fâil cem‘-i [6016] müennes-i sâlimdir.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r2.claim: The term can refer to horses, camels, or any running creatures.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r2.anchor: at, deve ve sâir koşanların hepsine ıtlak olunabilir.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r3.claim: As Besāʾir explains, the root ʿadw fundamentally means crossing or exceeding a limit; considered as movement, it gives ʿadw, running.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r3.anchor: bu “adv” maddesi esasen tecavüz mânasına mevzû‘dur. Gâh yürüyüş itibariyle mülâhaza edilir, ona “adv”, yani seğirtmek tâbir olunur.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r4.claim: Considered as an inward disposition, the root yields ʿadāwa and muʿādāt, hostility.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r4.anchor: Ve gâh kalbî olarak mülâhaza edilir, ona “adâvet” ve “mu‘âdât”, yani düşmanlık tâbir olunur.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r5.claim: Considered as injustice, the root yields ʿudwān, oppression and transgression.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r5.anchor: Gâh da adaleti ihlâl itibariyle mülâhaza edilir ona[^1] da “udvan”, yani zulüm ü te‘addî tâbir olunur.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r6.claim: Considered spatially, the root yields ʿadwā, contagion; the other meanings derive from these senses.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r6.anchor: Ve gâh da mekân ve mahal itibariyle mülâhaza edilir, ona da “advâ” yani sirâyet tâbir olunur. Sâir mânalar bundan müteferri‘dir.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r7.claim: In battle usage, ʿadī and ʿādiya name troops that habitually rush to attack.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r7.anchor: “Ganî” vezninde “adî” ve “sâriye” vezninde “âdiye” dâima harb u kıtâle koşup hücum eden cemaate denir.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r8.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r8.claim: Some restrict ʿadī to attacking infantry and ʿādiya to attacking cavalry.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r8.anchor: Bazıları “adî” piyade muhâcimlerine, “âdiye” süvari muhâcimlerine mahsus olduğunu söylemiştir.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r9.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r9.claim: A report from Ali interprets the runners as pilgrims’ camels going to Arafat.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r9.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’den mervî olarak Arafat’a giden huccâcın develeriyle tefsîrine dâir bir rivayet nakledilmiş

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r10.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas’s report identifies them as cavalry horses; Elmalılı says this is clear from the verses and is the choice of most exegetes.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r10.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan mervî olduğu üzere süvarilerin atları olmak âyetlerin mazmûnuna nazaran zâhirdir ve ekser müfessirîn bunu ihtiyar eylemişlerdir.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r11.claim: Dabḥ is the sound of horses’ rapid breathing while running, a huff.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r12.claim: This breathing is distinct from neighing and from the sound horses make on seeing food or their owner.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r12.anchor: “sahîl”[^4] denilen[^5] kişnemek değil, yemi ve sâhibini gördüğü zaman yaptığı gibi “hamhame” denilen sesi de değil

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r13.claim: Some say dabḥ occurs when either a horse or a dog runs.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r13.anchor: Denilmiştir ki “dabh” bir at, bir de köpek koşarken olur.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r14.claim: The phrase can be parsed as taḍbaḥu ḍabḥan or as dābiḥāt.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r14.anchor: Takdîr-i kelâm تضبح ضبحا veya “dâbihât” mânasındadır.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r19.claim: Those who read al-ʿādiyāt as pilgrims’ camels also explain al-mūriyāt as pilgrims who travel at night from Arafat to Muzdalifa and light a fire at the Sacred Monument.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r19.anchor: “âdiyât”ı huccâc develerine hamledenler de Arafat’tan geceleyin Müzdelife’ye Meş‘ar-ı Harâm’a gelip orada ateş yakan huccâc demişlerdir.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r23.claim: Elmalılı extends the image to modern fire-sparking weapons literally and, by extension, fast motorized assault vehicles; a Meccan dating, when Muslims had neither horses nor weapons, would make the future reference especially clear.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r23.anchor: o zaman İslâm’da ne at ne silah olmadığı cihetle bu âyetler bütün istikbâle ait demek olacağından bu mâna ve şümul daha vâzıhtır.

ELMALILI:100:1-2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r24.claim: The distinctive plural forms and successive faʾs suggest an ordered development of attack vehicles through the ages, encompassing motorized raiders as well as horses.
ELMALILI:100:1-2/r24.anchor: peyderpey tertip ifade eden fâ’larla îrad olundukları da mülâhaza olunursa

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:1/r1.claim: The oath depicts horses charging the enemy in battle, then swears by them because after humans they were the most important element of old warfare. It points to God as the giver of these useful, much-loved possessions and uses what people valued to stress the truth and importance of the following message.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:100:1/r1.anchor: Savaş sırasında düşman üzerine saldıran atlar tasvir edilmekte ve eski savaşların insandan sonra en önemli unsuru olması dolayısıyla atlar üzerine yemin edilmektedir.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234/r1.claim: Al-Bazzar, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim report from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet sent out horses; after a month without news, this verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p234/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خيلا ولبث شهرا لا يأتيه منها خبر فنزلت

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p463/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p463/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p463/r1.claim: Muqatil says the Prophet sent an expedition against a clan of Kinana under al-Mundhir ibn Amr al-Ansari; when news was delayed, hypocrites claimed all had been killed, so God revealed the horses in this verse.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p463/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: بعث رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - سرية إلى حي من كنانة واستعمل عليهم المنذر بن عمرو الأنصاري، فتأخر خبرهم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p463/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p463/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p463/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Messenger sent horses which ranged far for a month without news reaching him; the verse and the rest of the sura were then revealed, describing their nostril-breathing.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p463/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بعث خيلا فأسهبت شهرا لم يأته منها خبر، فنزلت: {والعاديات ضبحا} ضبحت بمناخرها، إلى آخر السورة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p463/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p463/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p463/r3.claim: Wahidi explains ashabat as traveling far across wide open plains; sahb is the singular of suhūb, meaning broad land.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p463/r3.anchor: ومعنى أسهبت: أمعنت في السهوب: وهي الأرض الواسعة جمع سهب.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p251/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p251/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p251/r1.claim: The opening horse-raid image recalls a familiar dawn attack that surprises people and scatters a group in dust, prefiguring the sudden, unseen Resurrection that catches the ungrateful unprepared and scatters people from their graves.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p251/r1.anchor: السورة تبدأ بالواو لافتة إلى ما عهد القوم من غارات الخيل المصبحة

KASHSHAF:100:5/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:5/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF:100:5/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās first glossed the chargers as horses, but ʿAlī summoned him and challenged his uninformed answer, noting that Badr had only two horses.
KASHSHAF:100:5/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : كنت جالساً في الحجر فجاء رجل فسألني عن { والعاديات ضَبْحاً ( 1 ) }

KASHSHAF:100:5/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:5/r9.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF:100:5/r9.claim: ʿAlī identified the chargers as camels travelling from ʿArafah to Muzdalifah and then Minā, and identified Jamʿ as Muzdalifah.
KASHSHAF:100:5/r9.anchor: فقال : ادعه لي ،   فلما وقفت على رأسه قال : تفتي الناس بما لا علم لك به

KASHSHAF:100:5/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:5/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:100:5/r10.claim: If the report is sound, ‘panting’ is transferred metaphorically to camels, just as bodily terms such as muzzle and hoof are transferred to humans.
KASHSHAF:100:5/r10.anchor: فإن صحّت الرواية فقد استعير الضبح للإبل ،   كما استعير المشافر والحافر للإنسان

KASHSHAF:100:5/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:5/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:100:5/r11.claim: Some hold that panting belongs only to horses, dogs, and foxes; another says it means the camels’ shoulders extending during travel, but that derivation is not established.
KASHSHAF:100:5/r11.anchor: وقيل : الضبح لا يكون إلاّ للفرس والكلب والثعلب .   وقيل : الضبح بمعنى الضبع

BAQILLANI:v1p52/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r5.speaker: زعموا
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r5.claim: They likewise call passages from al-ʿĀdiyāt and al-Dhāriyāt poetry, assigning the latter to al-basīṭ.

BURHAN:v2p114/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p114/r8.speaker: قالوا
BURHAN:v2p114/r8.claim: They classify the opening oath sequences of al-ʿAdiyat and al-Dhariyat as basit meter.
BURHAN:v2p114/r8.anchor: ﴿ والعاديات ضبحا فالموريات قدحا ﴾ ونحوه قوله

ITQAN:v1p57/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p57/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p57/r7.claim: Surat al-Adiyat and the cited passage in al-Anfal resemble Meccan revelation despite occurring in Medinan suras.
ITQAN:v1p57/r7.anchor: ومثال ما يشبه تنزيل مكة في السور المدنية قوله

NASHR:v1p299/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p299/r6.speaker: ابن خيرون عن خلاد
NASHR:v1p299/r6.claim: Ibn Khayrun uniquely reports Khallad assimilating the tāʾ in wa-l-ʿadiyati ḍabḥa.
NASHR:v1p299/r6.anchor: وانفرد ابن خيرون عنه بإدغام: والعاديات ضبحا

ITQAN:v1p45/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p45/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p45/r6.claim: Al-Adiyat has two classifications; the Medinan argument cites Ibn Abbas's report that a cavalry detachment was away for a month without news before the sura was revealed.
ITQAN:v1p45/r6.anchor: سورة العاديات فيها قولان ويستدل لكونها مدنية بما أخرجه الحاكم وغيره عن ابن عباس قال بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خيلا فلبثت شهرا لا يأتيه منها خبر فنزلت ﴿ والعاديات ﴾ الحديث

TAB:100:1/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:100:1/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the chargers as horses.
TAB:100:1/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله {  وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحا } قال :  الخيل ،

TAB:100:1/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:100:1/r2.claim: Mujāhid transmits Ibn ʿAbbās's view that the verse concerns horses in combat.
TAB:100:1/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ، في قول الله :  {  وَالْعَادِيَاتِ ضَبْحا } قال ابن عباس :  هو في القتال .

TAB:100:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:100:1/r3.claim: ʿIkrimah identifies the chargers as horses and explains the panting sound of a running horse.
TAB:100:1/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله {  وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحا } قال :  الخيل ،

TAB:100:1/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r4.speaker: عطاء
TAB:100:1/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says only dogs and horses among animals make this sound.
TAB:100:1/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج ، عن عطاء ، قال :  ليس شيء من الدوابّ يضبح غير الكلب والفرس .

TAB:100:1/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:100:1/r5.claim: Mujāhid says horses pant as they run.
TAB:100:1/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد ، في قوله الله :  {  وَالْعَادِيَاتِ ضَبْحا } قال :  الخيل تَضْبَح .

TAB:100:1/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:100:1/r6.claim: Qatādah says the horses ran until panting.
TAB:100:1/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله :  {  وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحا } قال :  هي الخيل ، عَدَتْ حَتى ضَبَحَتْ .

TAB:100:1/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r7.speaker: سالم
TAB:100:1/r7.claim: Sālim recites the verse as describing horses running panting.
TAB:100:1/r7.anchor: قال :  سمعت سالما يقرأ :  {  وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحا } قال :  هي الخيل عدت ضبحا .

TAB:100:1/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:100:1/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says no animal pants in this way except dog or horse.
TAB:100:1/r8.anchor: عن عطاء ، عن ابن عباس ، قال :  ما ضبحت دابة قطّ إلا كلب أو فرس .

TAB:100:1/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r9.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:100:1/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the chargers as horses.
TAB:100:1/r9.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  {  وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحا } قال :  هي الخيل .

TAB:100:1/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r10.speaker: عبد الله
TAB:100:1/r10.claim: ʿAbd Allāh identifies the chargers as camels.
TAB:100:1/r10.anchor: عن الأعمش ، عن إبراهيم ، عن عبد الله {  وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحا } قال :  هي الإبل .

TAB:100:1/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r11.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB:100:1/r11.claim: Ibrāhīm reports a camel interpretation, with camel breath distinguished from horse panting.
TAB:100:1/r11.anchor: عن منصور ، عن إبراهيم {  وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحا } قال :  الإبل .

TAB:100:1/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:100:1/r12.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports Ibn ʿAbbās initially said the chargers were horses raiding for God's cause.
TAB:100:1/r12.anchor: عن أبي معاوية البَجَليّ ، عن سعيد بن جُبَير ، عن ابن عباس ، حدثه قال :  بينما أنا في الحِجْر جالس

TAB:100:1/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r13.speaker: علي
TAB:100:1/r13.claim: ʿAlī rebukes Ibn ʿAbbās's horse view, noting Badr had only two horses, and says the chargers are pilgrims' camels; Ibn ʿAbbās retracts.
TAB:100:1/r13.anchor: فذهب إلى عليّ بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه وهو تحت سقاية زمزم ، فسأله عن الْعادِياتِ ضَبْحا

TAB:100:1/r14.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r14.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:100:1/r14.claim: Mujāhid attributes to Ibn Masʿūd the view that this concerns the Hajj.
TAB:100:1/r14.anchor: عن مجاهد ، في قول الله :  {  وَالْعَادِيَاتِ ضَبْحا } قال :  قال ابن مسعود :  هو في الحجّ .

TAB:100:1/r15.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r15.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB:100:1/r15.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr identifies the chargers as camels.
TAB:100:1/r15.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير ، قال :  هي الإبل ، يعني {  وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحا }

TAB:100:1/r16.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r16.speaker: author
TAB:100:1/r16.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers horses because camels do not make dabḥ, while horses do.
TAB:100:1/r16.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك عندي بالصواب :  قول من قال :  عني بالعاديات :  الخيل

TAB:100:1/r17.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r17.speaker: علي
TAB:100:1/r17.claim: ʿAlī distinguishes the sounds: horse dabḥ is panting and camel dabḥ is breathing.
TAB:100:1/r17.anchor: عن أبي صالح ، قال :  قال عليّ رضي الله عنه :  الضبح من الخيل :  الحمحمة

TAB:100:1/r18.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:100:1/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:100:1/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the sound as ‘aḥ aḥ.’
TAB:100:1/r18.anchor: عن عطاء ، قال :  سمعت ابن عباس يصف الضبح :  أَحْ أَحْ
